js:URLPattern:exec.description: The exec() method of the URLPattern interface takes a URL or object of URL parts, and returns either an object containing the results of matching the URL to the pattern, or null if the URL does not match the pattern.
js:URLPattern:exec.syntax: exec(input?: URLPatternInput, baseURL?: string | URL): URLPatternResult | null

js:URLPattern:test.description: The test() method of the URLPattern interface takes a URL string or object of URL parts, and returns a boolean indicating if the given input matches the current pattern.
js:URLPattern:test.syntax: test(input?: URLPatternInput, baseURL?: string | URL): boolean

js:URLSearchParams:size.description: The size read-only property of the URLSearchParams interface indicates the total number of search parameter entries.

js:URLSearchParams:append.description: The append() method of the URLSearchParams interface appends a specified key/value pair as a new search parameter.

js:URLSearchParams:delete.description: The delete() method of the URLSearchParams interface deletes specified parameters and their associated value(s) from the list of all search parameters.

js:URLSearchParams:get.description: The get() method of the URLSearchParams interface returns the first value associated to the given search parameter.

js:URLSearchParams:getAll.description: The getAll() method of the URLSearchParams interface returns all the values associated with a given search parameter as an array.

js:URLSearchParams:has.description: The has() method of the URLSearchParams interface returns a boolean value that indicates whether the specified parameter is in the search parameters.

js:URLSearchParams:set.description: The set() method of the URLSearchParams interface sets the value associated with a given search parameter to the given value. If there were several matching values, this method deletes the others. If the search parameter doesn't exist, this method creates it.

js:URLSearchParams:sort.description: The URLSearchParams.sort() method sorts all key/value pairs contained in this object in place and returns undefined. Key/value pairs are sorted by the values of the UTF-16 code units of the keys. This method uses a stable sorting algorithm (i.e., the relative order between key/value pairs with equal keys will be preserved).

js:UserActivation:hasBeenActive.description: The read-only hasBeenActive property of the UserActivation interface indicates whether the current window has sticky user activation.

js:UserActivation:isActive.description: The read-only isActive property of the UserActivation interface indicates whether the current window has transient user activation.

js:VTTCue:align.description: The align property of the VTTCue interface represents the alignment of all of the lines of text in the text box.

js:VTTCue:line.description: The line property of the VTTCue interface represents the cue line of this WebVTT cue.

js:VTTCue:lineAlign.description: The lineAlign property of the VTTCue interface represents the alignment of this VTT cue.

js:VTTCue:position.description: The position property of the VTTCue interface represents the indentation of the cue within the line.

js:VTTCue:positionAlign.description: The positionAlign property of the VTTCue interface is used to determine what VTTCue.position is anchored to.

js:VTTCue:region.description: The region property of the VTTCue interface returns and sets the VTTRegion that this cue belongs to.

js:VTTCue:size.description: The size property of the VTTCue interface represents the size of the cue as a percentage of the video size.

js:VTTCue:snapToLines.description: The snapToLines property of the VTTCue interface is a Boolean indicating if the VTTCue.line property is an integer number of lines, or a percentage of the video size.

js:VTTCue:text.description: The text property of the VTTCue interface represents the text contents of the cue.

js:VTTCue:vertical.description: The vertical property of the VTTCue interface is a string representing the cue's writing direction.

js:VTTCue:getCueAsHTML.description: The getCueAsHTML() method of the VTTCue interface returns a DocumentFragment containing the cue content.

js:ValidityState:badInput.description: The read-only badInput property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the user has provided input that the browser is unable to convert. For example, if you have a number input element whose content is a string.

js:ValidityState:customError.description: The read-only customError property of the ValidityState interface returns true if an element doesn't meet the validation required in the custom validity set by the element's setCustomValidity() method.

js:ValidityState:patternMismatch.description: The read-only patternMismatch property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, after having been edited by the user, does not conform to the constraints set by the element's pattern attribute.

js:ValidityState:rangeOverflow.description: The read-only rangeOverflow property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, after having been edited by the user, does not conform to the constraints set by the element's max attribute.

js:ValidityState:rangeUnderflow.description: The read-only rangeUnderflow property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, after having been edited by the user, does not conform to the constraints set by the element's min attribute.

js:ValidityState:stepMismatch.description: The read-only stepMismatch property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, after having been edited by the user, does not conform to the constraints set by the element's step attribute.

js:ValidityState:tooLong.description: The read-only tooLong property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input> or <textarea>, after having been edited by the user, exceeds the maximum code-unit length established by the element's maxlength attribute.

js:ValidityState:tooShort.description: The read-only tooShort property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, <button>, <select>, <output>, <fieldset> or <textarea>, after having been edited by the user, is less than the minimum code-unit length established by the element's minlength attribute.

js:ValidityState:typeMismatch.description: The read-only typeMismatch property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input>, after having been edited by the user, does not conform to the constraints set by the element's type attribute.

js:ValidityState:valid.description: The read-only valid property of the ValidityState interface indicates if the value of an <input> element meets all its validation constraints, and is therefore considered to be valid.

js:ValidityState:valueMissing.description: The read-only valueMissing property of the ValidityState interface indicates if a required control, such as an <input>, <select>, or <textarea>, has an empty value.

js:VideoColorSpace:fullRange.description: The fullRange read-only property of the VideoColorSpace interface returns true if full-range color values are used.

js:VideoColorSpace:matrix.description: The matrix read-only property of the VideoColorSpace interface returns the matrix coefficient of the video. Matrix coefficients describe the relationship between sample component values and color coordinates.

js:VideoColorSpace:primaries.description: The primaries read-only property of the VideoColorSpace interface returns the color gamut of the video.

js:VideoColorSpace:transfer.description: The transfer read-only property of the VideoColorSpace interface returns the opto-electronic transfer characteristics of the video.

js:VideoColorSpace:toJSON.description: The toJSON() method of the VideoColorSpace interface is a serializer that returns a JSON representation of the VideoColorSpace object.

js:VideoDecoder:decodeQueueSize.description: The decodeQueueSize read-only property of the VideoDecoder interface returns the number of pending decode requests in the queue.

js:VideoDecoder:state.description: The state property of the VideoDecoder interface returns the current state of the underlying codec.

js:VideoDecoder:close.description: The close() method of the VideoDecoder interface ends all pending work and releases system resources.

js:VideoDecoder:configure.description: The configure() method of the VideoDecoder interface enqueues a control message to configure the video decoder for decoding chunks.

js:VideoDecoder:decode.description: The decode() method of the VideoDecoder interface enqueues a control message to decode a given chunk of video.

js:VideoDecoder:flush.description: The flush() method of the VideoDecoder interface returns a Promise that resolves once all pending messages in the queue have been completed.

js:VideoDecoder:reset.description: The reset() method of the VideoDecoder interface resets all states including configuration, control messages in the control message queue, and all pending callbacks.

js:VideoEncoder:encodeQueueSize.description: The encodeQueueSize read-only property of the VideoEncoder interface returns the number of pending encode requests in the queue.

js:VideoEncoder:state.description: The state read-only property of the VideoEncoder interface returns the current state of the underlying codec.

js:VideoEncoder:close.description: The close() method of the VideoEncoder interface ends all pending work and releases system resources.

js:VideoEncoder:configure.description: The configure() method of the VideoEncoder interface changes the state of the encoder to "configured" and asynchronously prepares the encoder to accept VideoEncoders for encoding with the specified parameters. If the encoder doesn't support the specified parameters or can't be initialized for other reasons an error will be reported via the error callback provided to the VideoEncoder constructor.

js:VideoEncoder:encode.description: The encode() method of the VideoEncoder interface asynchronously encodes a VideoFrame. Encoded data (EncodedVideoChunk) or an error will eventually be returned via the callbacks provided to the VideoEncoder constructor.

js:VideoEncoder:flush.description: The flush() method of the VideoEncoder interface forces all pending encodes to complete.

js:VideoEncoder:reset.description: The reset() method of the VideoEncoder interface synchronously cancels all pending encodes and callbacks, frees all underlying resources and sets the state to "unconfigured". After calling reset(), configure() must be called before resuming encode() calls.

js:VideoFrame:codedHeight.description: The codedHeight property of the VideoFrame interface returns the height of the VideoFrame in pixels, potentially including non-visible padding, and prior to considering potential ratio adjustments.

js:VideoFrame:codedRect.description: The codedRect property of the VideoFrame interface returns a DOMRectReadOnly with the width and height matching VideoFrame.codedWidth and VideoFrame.codedHeight.

js:VideoFrame:codedWidth.description: The codedWidth property of the VideoFrame interface returns the width of the VideoFrame in pixels, potentially including non-visible padding, and prior to considering potential ratio adjustments.

js:VideoFrame:colorSpace.description: The colorSpace property of the VideoFrame interface returns a VideoColorSpace object representing the color space of the video.

js:VideoFrame:displayHeight.description: The displayHeight property of the VideoFrame interface returns the height of the VideoFrame after applying aspect ratio adjustments.

js:VideoFrame:displayWidth.description: The displayWidth property of the VideoFrame interface returns the width of the VideoFrame after applying aspect ratio adjustments.

js:VideoFrame:duration.description: The duration property of the VideoFrame interface returns an integer indicating the duration of the video in microseconds.

js:VideoFrame:format.description: The format property of the VideoFrame interface returns the pixel format of the VideoFrame.

js:VideoFrame:timestamp.description: The timestamp property of the VideoFrame interface returns an integer indicating the timestamp of the video in microseconds.

js:VideoFrame:visibleRect.description: The visibleRect property of the VideoFrame interface returns a DOMRectReadOnly describing the visible rectangle of pixels for this VideoFrame.

js:VideoFrame:allocationSize.description: The allocationSize() method of the VideoFrame interface returns the number of bytes required to hold the video as filtered by options passed into the method.

js:VideoFrame:clone.description: The clone() method of the VideoFrame interface creates a new VideoFrame object referencing the same media resource as the original.

js:VideoFrame:close.description: The close() method of the VideoFrame interface clears all states and releases the reference to the media resource.

js:VideoFrame:copyTo.description: The copyTo() method of the VideoFrame interface copies the contents of the VideoFrame to an ArrayBuffer.

js:VideoPlaybackQuality:corruptedVideoFr.description:
The VideoPlaybackQuality interface's read-only corruptedVideoFrames property the number of corrupted video frames that have been received since the <video> element was last loaded or reloaded.
@deprecated

js:VideoPlaybackQuality:creationTime.description: The read-only creationTime property on the VideoPlaybackQuality interface reports the number of milliseconds since the browsing context was created this quality sample was recorded.

js:VideoPlaybackQuality:droppedVideoFram.description: The read-only droppedVideoFrames property of the VideoPlaybackQuality interface returns the number of video frames which have been dropped rather than being displayed since the last time the media was loaded into the HTMLVideoElement.

js:VideoPlaybackQuality:totalVideoFrames.description: The VideoPlaybackQuality interface's totalVideoFrames read-only property returns the total number of video frames that have been displayed or dropped since the media was loaded.

js:ViewTimeline:endOffset.description: The endOffset read-only property of the ViewTimeline interface returns a CSSNumericValue representing the ending (100% progress) scroll position of the timeline as an offset from the start of the overflowing section of content in the scroller.

js:ViewTimeline:startOffset.description: The startOffset read-only property of the ViewTimeline interface returns a CSSNumericValue representing the starting (0% progress) scroll position of the timeline as an offset from the start of the overflowing section of content in the scroller.

js:ViewTimeline:subject.description: The subject read-only property of the ViewTimeline interface returns a reference to the subject element whose visibility within its nearest ancestor scrollable element (scroller) is driving the progress of the timeline.

js:ViewTransition:finished.description: The finished read-only property of the ViewTransition interface is a Promise that fulfills once the transition animation is finished, and the new page view is visible and interactive to the user.

js:ViewTransition:ready.description: The ready read-only property of the ViewTransition interface is a Promise that fulfills once the pseudo-element tree is created and the transition animation is about to start.

js:ViewTransition:types.description: The types read-only property of the ViewTransition interface is a ViewTransitionTypeSet that allows the types set on the view transition to be accessed and modified.

js:ViewTransition:updateCallbackDone.description: The updateCallbackDone read-only property of the ViewTransition interface is a Promise that fulfills when the promise returned by the document.startViewTransition() method's callback fulfills, or rejects when it rejects.

js:ViewTransition:skipTransition.description: The skipTransition() method of the ViewTransition interface skips the animation part of the view transition, but doesn't skip running the associated view update.

js:VisualViewport:height.description: The height read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the height of the visual viewport, in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:VisualViewport:offsetLeft.description: The offsetLeft read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the offset of the left edge of the visual viewport from the left edge of the layout viewport in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:VisualViewport:offsetTop.description: The offsetTop read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the offset of the top edge of the visual viewport from the top edge of the layout viewport in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:VisualViewport:pageLeft.description: The pageLeft read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the x coordinate of the left edge of the visual viewport relative to the initial containing block origin, in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:VisualViewport:pageTop.description: The pageTop read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the y coordinate of the top edge of the visual viewport relative to the initial containing block origin, in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:VisualViewport:scale.description: The scale read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the pinch-zoom scaling factor applied to the visual viewport, or 0 if current document is not fully active, or 1 if there is no output device.

js:VisualViewport:width.description: The width read-only property of the VisualViewport interface returns the width of the visual viewport, in CSS pixels, or 0 if current document is not fully active.

js:WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc:getSupp.description: The WEBGL_compressed_texture_astc.getSupportedProfiles() method returns an array of strings containing the names of the ASTC profiles supported by the implementation.

js:WEBGL_debug_shaders:getTranslatedShad.description: The WEBGL_debug_shaders.getTranslatedShaderSource() method is part of the WebGL API and allows you to debug a translated shader.

js:WEBGL_draw_buffers:drawBuffersWEBGL.description: The WEBGL_draw_buffers.drawBuffersWEBGL() method is part of the WebGL API and allows you to define the draw buffers to which all fragment colors are written.

js:WEBGL_lose_context:loseContext.description: The loseContext() method of the WEBGL_lose_context extension is part of the WebGL API and allows you to simulate losing the context of a WebGLRenderingContext.

js:WEBGL_lose_context:restoreContext.description: The restoreContext() method of the WEBGL_lose_context extension is part of the WebGL API and allows you to simulate restoring the context of a WebGLRenderingContext.

js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawArraysInsta.description: The WEBGL_multi_draw.multiDrawArraysInstancedWEBGL() method of the WebGL API renders multiple primitives from array data. It is identical to multiple calls to the gl.drawArraysInstanced() method.
js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawArraysInsta.syntax: multiDrawArraysInstancedWEBGL(mode: GLenum, firstsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLint[], firstsOffset: number, countsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], countsOffset: number, instanceCountsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], instanceCountsOffset: number, drawcount: GLsizei): void

js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawArraysWEBGL.description: The WEBGL_multi_draw.multiDrawArraysWEBGL() method of the WebGL API renders multiple primitives from array data. It is identical to multiple calls to the gl.drawArrays() method.
js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawArraysWEBGL.syntax: multiDrawArraysWEBGL(mode: GLenum, firstsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLint[], firstsOffset: number, countsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], countsOffset: number, drawcount: GLsizei): void

js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawElementsIns.description: The WEBGL_multi_draw.multiDrawElementsInstancedWEBGL() method of the WebGL API renders multiple primitives from array data. It is identical to multiple calls to the gl.drawElementsInstanced() method.
js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawElementsIns.syntax: multiDrawElementsInstancedWEBGL(mode: GLenum, countsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], countsOffset: number, type: GLenum, offsetsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], offsetsOffset: number, instanceCountsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], instanceCountsOffset: number, drawcount: GLsizei): void

js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawElementsWEB.description: The WEBGL_multi_draw.multiDrawElementsWEBGL() method of the WebGL API renders multiple primitives from array data. It is identical to multiple calls to the gl.drawElements() method.
js:WEBGL_multi_draw:multiDrawElementsWEB.syntax: multiDrawElementsWEBGL(mode: GLenum, countsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], countsOffset: number, type: GLenum, offsetsList: Int32Array<ArrayBufferLike> | GLsizei[], offsetsOffset: number, drawcount: GLsizei): void

js:WakeLock:request.description: The request() method of the WakeLock interface returns a Promise that fulfills with a WakeLockSentinel object if the system screen wake lock is granted.

js:WakeLockSentinel:released.description: The released read-only property of the WakeLockSentinel interface returns a boolean that indicates whether a WakeLockSentinel has been released.

js:WakeLockSentinel:type.description: The type read-only property of the WakeLockSentinel interface returns a string representation of the currently acquired WakeLockSentinel type.

js:WakeLockSentinel:release.description: The release() method of the WakeLockSentinel interface releases the WakeLockSentinel, returning a Promise that is resolved once the sentinel has been successfully released.

js:WaveShaperNode:curve.description: The curve property of the WaveShaperNode interface is a Float32Array of numbers describing the distortion to apply.

js:WaveShaperNode:oversample.description: The oversample property of the WaveShaperNode interface is an enumerated value indicating if oversampling must be used. Oversampling is a technique for creating more samples (up-sampling) before applying a distortion effect to the audio signal.

js:WebGLActiveInfo:name.description: The read-only WebGLActiveInfo.name property represents the name of the requested data returned by calling the getActiveAttrib() or getActiveUniform() methods.

js:WebGLActiveInfo:size.description: The read-only WebGLActiveInfo.size property is a Number representing the size of the requested data returned by calling the getActiveAttrib() or getActiveUniform() methods.

js:WebGLActiveInfo:type.description: The read-only WebGLActiveInfo.type property represents the type of the requested data returned by calling the getActiveAttrib() or getActiveUniform() methods.

js:WebGLContextEvent:statusMessage.description: The read-only WebGLContextEvent.statusMessage property contains additional event status information, or is an empty string if no additional information is available.

js:WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat:precision.description: The read-only WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat.precision property returns the number of bits of precision that can be represented.

js:WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat:rangeMax.description: The read-only WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat.rangeMax property returns the base 2 log of the absolute value of the maximum value that can be represented.

js:WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat:rangeMin.description: The read-only WebGLShaderPrecisionFormat.rangeMin property returns the base 2 log of the absolute value of the minimum value that can be represented.

js:WebSocket:binaryType.description: The WebSocket.binaryType property controls the type of binary data being received over the WebSocket connection.

js:WebSocket:bufferedAmount.description: The WebSocket.bufferedAmount read-only property returns the number of bytes of data that have been queued using calls to send() but not yet transmitted to the network. This value resets to zero once all queued data has been sent. This value does not reset to zero when the connection is closed; if you keep calling send(), this will continue to climb.

js:WebSocket:extensions.description: The WebSocket.extensions read-only property returns the extensions selected by the server. This is currently only the empty string or a list of extensions as negotiated by the connection.

js:WebSocket:protocol.description: The WebSocket.protocol read-only property returns the name of the sub-protocol the server selected; this will be one of the strings specified in the protocols parameter when creating the WebSocket object, or the empty string if no connection is established.

js:WebSocket:readyState.description: The WebSocket.readyState read-only property returns the current state of the WebSocket connection.

js:WebSocket:url.description: The WebSocket.url read-only property returns the absolute URL of the WebSocket as resolved by the constructor.

js:WebSocket:close.description: The WebSocket.close() method closes the WebSocket connection or connection attempt, if any. If the connection is already CLOSED, this method does nothing.

js:WebSocket:send.description: The WebSocket.send() method enqueues the specified data to be transmitted to the server over the WebSocket connection, increasing the value of bufferedAmount by the number of bytes needed to contain the data. If the data can't be sent (for example, because it needs to be buffered but the buffer is full), the socket is closed automatically. The browser will throw an exception if you call send() when the connection is in the CONNECTING state. If you call send() when the connection is in the CLOSING or CLOSED states, the browser will silently discard the data.

js:WebTransport:closed.description: The closed read-only property of the WebTransport interface returns a promise that resolves when the transport is closed.

js:WebTransport:congestionControl.description: The congestionControl read-only property of the WebTransport interface indicates the application's preference for either high throughput or low-latency when sending data.

js:WebTransport:datagrams.description: The datagrams read-only property of the WebTransport interface returns a WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream instance that can be used to send and receive datagrams — unreliable data transmission.

js:WebTransport:incomingBidirectionalStr.description: The incomingBidirectionalStreams read-only property of the WebTransport interface represents one or more bidirectional streams opened by the server. Returns a ReadableStream of WebTransportBidirectionalStream objects. Each one can be used to reliably read data from the server and write data back to it.

js:WebTransport:incomingUnidirectionalSt.description: The incomingUnidirectionalStreams read-only property of the WebTransport interface represents one or more unidirectional streams opened by the server. Returns a ReadableStream of WebTransportReceiveStream objects. Each one can be used to reliably read data from the server.

js:WebTransport:ready.description: The ready read-only property of the WebTransport interface returns a promise that resolves when the transport is ready to use.

js:WebTransport:reliability.description: The reliability read-only property of the WebTransport interface indicates whether the connection supports reliable transports only, or whether it also supports unreliable transports (such as UDP).

js:WebTransport:close.description: The close() method of the WebTransport interface closes an ongoing WebTransport session.

js:WebTransport:createBidirectionalStrea.description: The createBidirectionalStream() method of the WebTransport interface asynchronously opens and returns a bidirectional stream.

js:WebTransport:createUnidirectionalStre.description: The createUnidirectionalStream() method of the WebTransport interface asynchronously opens a unidirectional stream.

js:WebTransport:getStats.description: The getStats() method of the WebTransport interface asynchronously returns an object containing HTTP/3 connection statistics.

js:WebTransportBidirectionalStream:reada.description: The readable read-only property of the WebTransportBidirectionalStream interface returns a WebTransportReceiveStream instance that can be used to reliably read incoming data.

js:WebTransportBidirectionalStream:writa.description: The writable read-only property of the WebTransportBidirectionalStream interface returns a WebTransportSendStream instance that can be used to write outgoing data.

js:WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream:inco.description: The incomingHighWaterMark property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface gets or sets the high water mark for incoming chunks of data — this is the maximum size, in chunks, that the incoming ReadableStream's internal queue can reach before it is considered full. See Internal queues and queuing strategies for more information.
The incomingMaxAge property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface gets or sets the maximum age for incoming datagrams, in milliseconds.

js:WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream:maxD.description: The maxDatagramSize read-only property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface returns the maximum allowable size of outgoing datagrams, in bytes, that can be written to writable.

js:WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream:outg.description: The outgoingHighWaterMark property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface gets or sets the high water mark for outgoing chunks of data — this is the maximum size, in chunks, that the outgoing WritableStream's internal queue can reach before it is considered full. See Internal queues and queuing strategies for more information.
The outgoingMaxAge property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface gets or sets the maximum age for outgoing datagrams, in milliseconds.

js:WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream:read.description: The readable read-only property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface returns a ReadableStream instance that can be used to unreliably read incoming datagrams from the stream.

js:WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream:writ.description: The writable read-only property of the WebTransportDatagramDuplexStream interface returns a WritableStream instance that can be used to unreliably write outgoing datagrams to the stream.

js:WebTransportError:source.description: The source read-only property of the WebTransportError interface returns an enumerated value indicating the source of the error.

js:WebTransportError:streamErrorCode.description: The streamErrorCode read-only property of the WebTransportError interface returns a number in the range 0-255 indicating the application protocol error code for this error, or null if one is not available.

js:WebTransportReceiveStream:getStats.description: The getStats() method of the WebTransportReceiveStream interface asynchronously returns an object containing statistics for the current stream.

js:WebTransportSendStream:sendOrder.description: The sendOrder property of the WebTransportSendStream interface indicates the send priority of this stream relative to other streams for which the value has been set.

js:WebTransportSendStream:getStats.description: The getStats() method of the WebTransportSendStream interface asynchronously returns an object containing statistics for the current stream.

js:WheelEvent:deltaMode.description: The WheelEvent.deltaMode read-only property returns an unsigned long representing the unit of the delta values scroll amount. Permitted values are:

js:WheelEvent:deltaX.description: The WheelEvent.deltaX read-only property is a double representing the horizontal scroll amount in the WheelEvent.deltaMode unit.

js:WheelEvent:deltaY.description: The WheelEvent.deltaY read-only property is a double representing the vertical scroll amount in the WheelEvent.deltaMode unit.

js:WheelEvent:deltaZ.description: The WheelEvent.deltaZ read-only property is a double representing the scroll amount along the z-axis, in the WheelEvent.deltaMode unit.

js:Window:clientInformation.description: @deprecated This is a legacy alias of navigator.

js:Window:closed.description: The Window.closed read-only property indicates whether the referenced window is closed or not.

js:Window:cookieStore.description: The cookieStore read-only property of the Window interface returns a reference to the CookieStore object for the current document context. This is an entry point for the Cookie Store API.

js:Window:customElements.description: The customElements read-only property of the Window interface returns a reference to the global CustomElementRegistry object, which can be used to register new custom elements and get information about previously registered custom elements.

js:Window:devicePixelRatio.description: The devicePixelRatio of Window interface returns the ratio of the resolution in physical pixels to the resolution in CSS pixels for the current display device.

js:Window:document.description: window.document returns a reference to the document contained in the window.

js:Window:documentPictureInPicture.description:
The documentPictureInPicture read-only property of the Window interface returns a reference to the DocumentPictureInPicture object for the current document context.
Available only in secure contexts.

js:Window:event.description:
The read-only Window property event returns the Event which is currently being handled by the site's code. Outside the context of an event handler, the value is always undefined.
@deprecated

js:Window:external.description:
The external property of the Window API returns an instance of the External interface, which was intended to contain functions related to adding external search providers to the browser. However, this is now deprecated, and the contained methods are now dummy functions that do nothing as per spec.
@deprecated

js:Window:frameElement.description: The Window.frameElement property returns the element (such as <iframe> or <object>) in which the window is embedded.

js:Window:frames.description: Returns the window itself, which is an array-like object, listing the direct sub-frames of the current window.

js:Window:history.description: The Window.history read-only property returns a reference to the History object, which provides an interface for manipulating the browser session history (pages visited in the tab or frame that the current page is loaded in).

js:Window:innerHeight.description: The read-only innerHeight property of the Window interface returns the interior height of the window in pixels, including the height of the horizontal scroll bar, if present.

js:Window:innerWidth.description: The read-only Window property innerWidth returns the interior width of the window in pixels (that is, the width of the window's layout viewport). That includes the width of the vertical scroll bar, if one is present.

js:Window:length.description: Returns the number of frames (either <frame> or <iframe> elements) in the window.

js:Window:get.description: The read-only location property of the Window interface returns a Location object with information about the current location of the document.

js:Window:name.description: The Window.name property gets/sets the name of the window's browsing context.

js:Window:navigation.description: The navigation read-only property of the Window interface returns the current window's associated Navigation object.

js:Window:navigator.description: The Window.navigator read-only property returns a reference to the Navigator object, which has methods and properties about the application running the script.

js:Window:ondevicemotion.syntax: ondevicemotion: ((this: Window, ev: DeviceMotionEvent) => any) | null

js:Window:ondeviceorientation.syntax: ondeviceorientation: ((this: Window, ev: DeviceOrientationEvent) => any) | null

js:Window:ondeviceorientationabsolute.syntax: ondeviceorientationabsolute: ((this: Window, ev: DeviceOrientationEvent) => any) | null

js:Window:onorientationchange.syntax: onorientationchange: ((this: Window, ev: Event) => any) | null

js:Window:opener.description: The Window interface's opener property returns a reference to the window that opened the window, either with open(), or by navigating a link with a target attribute.

js:Window:orientation.description:
Returns the orientation in degrees (in 90-degree increments) of the viewport relative to the device's natural orientation.
@deprecated

js:Window:originAgentCluster.description: The originAgentCluster read-only property of the Window interface returns true if this window belongs to an origin-keyed agent cluster: this means that the operating system has provided dedicated resources (for example an operating system process) to this window's origin that are not shared with windows from other origins.

js:Window:outerHeight.description: The Window.outerHeight read-only property returns the height in pixels of the whole browser window, including any sidebar, window chrome, and window-resizing borders/handles.

js:Window:outerWidth.description: Window.outerWidth read-only property returns the width of the outside of the browser window. It represents the width of the whole browser window including sidebar (if expanded), window chrome and window resizing borders/handles.

js:Window:parent.description: The Window.parent property is a reference to the parent of the current window or subframe.

js:Window:screen.description: The Window property screen returns a reference to the screen object associated with the window. The screen object, implementing the Screen interface, is a special object for inspecting properties of the screen on which the current window is being rendered.

js:Window:screenLeft.description: The Window.screenLeft read-only property returns the horizontal distance, in CSS pixels, from the left border of the user's browser viewport to the left side of the screen.

js:Window:screenTop.description: The Window.screenTop read-only property returns the vertical distance, in CSS pixels, from the top border of the user's browser viewport to the top side of the screen.

js:Window:screenX.description: The Window.screenX read-only property returns the horizontal distance, in CSS pixels, of the left border of the user's browser viewport to the left side of the screen.

js:Window:screenY.description: The Window.screenY read-only property returns the vertical distance, in CSS pixels, of the top border of the user's browser viewport to the top edge of the screen.

js:Window:scrollX.description: The read-only scrollX property of the Window interface returns the number of pixels by which the document is currently scrolled horizontally. This value is subpixel precise in modern browsers, meaning that it isn't necessarily a whole number. You can get the number of pixels the document is scrolled vertically from the scrollY property.

js:Window:scrollY.description: The read-only scrollY property of the Window interface returns the number of pixels by which the document is currently scrolled vertically. This value is subpixel precise in modern browsers, meaning that it isn't necessarily a whole number. You can get the number of pixels the document is scrolled horizontally from the scrollX property.

js:Window:self.description: The Window.self read-only property returns the window itself, as a WindowProxy. It can be used with dot notation on a window object (that is, window.self) or standalone (self). The advantage of the standalone notation is that a similar notation exists for non-window contexts, such as in Web Workers. By using self, you can refer to the global scope in a way that will work not only in a window context (self will resolve to window.self) but also in a worker context (self will then resolve to WorkerGlobalScope.self).

js:Window:speechSynthesis.description: The speechSynthesis read-only property of the Window object returns a SpeechSynthesis object, which is the entry point into using Web Speech API speech synthesis functionality.

js:Window:status.description:
The status property of the Window interface was originally intended to set the text in the status bar at the bottom of the browser window. However, the HTML standard now requires setting window.status to have no effect on the text displayed in the status bar.
@deprecated

js:Window:top.description: Returns a reference to the topmost window in the window hierarchy.

js:Window:visualViewport.description: The visualViewport read-only property of the Window interface returns a VisualViewport object representing the visual viewport for a given window, or null if current document is not fully active.

js:Window:window.description: The window property of a Window object points to the window object itself.

js:Window:alert.description: window.alert() instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message, and to wait until the user dismisses the dialog.

js:Window:cancelIdleCallback.description: The window.cancelIdleCallback() method cancels a callback previously scheduled with window.requestIdleCallback().

js:Window:captureEvents.description:
The Window.captureEvents() method does nothing. Its original behavior has been removed from the specification, but the method itself has been retained so as not to break code that calls it.
@deprecated

js:Window:close.description: The Window.close() method closes the current window, or the window on which it was called.

js:Window:confirm.description: window.confirm() instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message, and to wait until the user either confirms or cancels the dialog.

js:Window:focus.description: Makes a request to bring the window to the front. It may fail due to user settings and the window isn't guaranteed to be frontmost before this method returns.

js:Window:getComputedStyle.description: The Window.getComputedStyle() method returns a live read-only CSSStyleProperties object containing the resolved values of all CSS properties of an element, after applying active stylesheets and resolving any computation those values may contain.
js:Window:getComputedStyle.syntax: getComputedStyle(elt: Element, pseudoElt?: string | null): CSSStyleDeclaration

js:Window:getSelection.description: The getSelection() method of the Window interface returns the Selection object associated with the window's document, representing the range of text selected by the user or the current position of the caret.

js:Window:matchMedia.description: The Window interface's matchMedia() method returns a new MediaQueryList object that can then be used to determine if the document matches the media query string, as well as to monitor the document to detect when it matches (or stops matching) that media query.

js:Window:moveBy.description: The moveBy() method of the Window interface moves the current window by a specified amount.

js:Window:moveTo.description: The moveTo() method of the Window interface moves the current window to the specified coordinates.

js:Window:open.description: The open() method of the Window interface loads a specified resource into a new or existing browsing context (that is, a tab, a window, or an iframe) under a specified name.
js:Window:open.syntax: open(url?: string | URL, target?: string, features?: string): WindowProxy | null

js:Window:postMessage.description: The window.postMessage() method safely enables cross-origin communication between Window objects; e.g., between a page and a pop-up that it spawned, or between a page and an iframe embedded within it.
js:Window:postMessage.syntax: postMessage(message: any, targetOrigin: string, transfer?: Transferable[]): void

js:Window:print.description: Opens the print dialog to print the current document.

js:Window:prompt.description: window.prompt() instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message prompting the user to input some text, and to wait until the user either submits the text or cancels the dialog.

js:Window:releaseEvents.description:
Releases the window from trapping events of a specific type.
@deprecated

js:Window:requestIdleCallback.description: The window.requestIdleCallback() method queues a function to be called during a browser's idle periods. This enables developers to perform background and low priority work on the main thread, without impacting latency-critical events such as animation and input response. Functions are generally called in first-in-first-out order; however, callbacks which have a timeout specified may be called out-of-order if necessary in order to run them before the timeout elapses.

js:Window:resizeBy.description: The Window.resizeBy() method resizes the current window by a specified amount.

js:Window:resizeTo.description: The Window.resizeTo() method dynamically resizes the window.

js:Window:scroll.description: The Window.scroll() method scrolls the window to a particular place in the document.

js:Window:scrollBy.description: The Window.scrollBy() method scrolls the document in the window by the given amount.

js:Window:scrollTo.description: Window.scrollTo() scrolls to a particular set of coordinates in the document.

js:Window:stop.description: The window.stop() stops further resource loading in the current browsing context, equivalent to the stop button in the browser.

js:WindowEventHandlers:onunload.description: @deprecated The unload event is not reliable, consider visibilitychange or pagehide events.
js:WindowEventHandlers:onunload.syntax: onunload: ((this: WindowEventHandlers, ev: Event) => any) | null

js:Worker:postMessage.description: The postMessage() method of the Worker interface sends a message to the worker. The first parameter is the data to send to the worker. The data may be any JavaScript object that can be handled by the structured clone algorithm.

js:Worker:terminate.description: The terminate() method of the Worker interface immediately terminates the Worker. This does not offer the worker an opportunity to finish its operations; it is stopped at once.

js:Worklet:addModule.description: The addModule() method of the Worklet interface loads the module in the given JavaScript file and adds it to the current Worklet.
js:Worklet:addModule.syntax: addModule(moduleURL: string | URL, options?: WorkletOptions): Promise<void>

js:WritableStream:locked.description: The locked read-only property of the WritableStream interface returns a boolean indicating whether the WritableStream is locked to a writer.

js:WritableStream:abort.description: The abort() method of the WritableStream interface aborts the stream, signaling that the producer can no longer successfully write to the stream and it is to be immediately moved to an error state, with any queued writes discarded.

js:WritableStream:close.description: The close() method of the WritableStream interface closes the associated stream. All chunks written before this method is called are sent before the returned promise is fulfilled.

js:WritableStream:getWriter.description: The getWriter() method of the WritableStream interface returns a new instance of WritableStreamDefaultWriter and locks the stream to that instance. While the stream is locked, no other writer can be acquired until this one is released.

js:WritableStreamDefaultController:signa.description: The read-only signal property of the WritableStreamDefaultController interface returns the AbortSignal associated with the controller.

js:WritableStreamDefaultController:error.description: The error() method of the WritableStreamDefaultController interface causes any future interactions with the associated stream to error.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:closed.description: The closed read-only property of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface returns a Promise that fulfills if the stream becomes closed, or rejects if the stream errors or the writer's lock is released.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:desiredSi.description: The desiredSize read-only property of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface returns the desired size required to fill the stream's internal queue.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:ready.description: The ready read-only property of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface returns a Promise that resolves when the desired size of the stream's internal queue transitions from non-positive to positive, signaling that it is no longer applying backpressure.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:abort.description: The abort() method of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface aborts the stream, signaling that the producer can no longer successfully write to the stream and it is to be immediately moved to an error state, with any queued writes discarded.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:close.description: The close() method of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface closes the associated writable stream.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:releaseLo.description: The releaseLock() method of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface releases the writer's lock on the corresponding stream. After the lock is released, the writer is no longer active. If the associated stream is errored when the lock is released, the writer will appear errored in the same way from now on; otherwise, the writer will appear closed.

js:WritableStreamDefaultWriter:write.description: The write() method of the WritableStreamDefaultWriter interface writes a passed chunk of data to a WritableStream and its underlying sink, then returns a Promise that resolves to indicate the success or failure of the write operation.

js:XMLHttpRequest:readyState.description: The XMLHttpRequest.readyState property returns the state an XMLHttpRequest client is in. An XHR client exists in one of the following states:

js:XMLHttpRequest:response.description: The XMLHttpRequest response property returns the response's body content as an ArrayBuffer, a Blob, a Document, a JavaScript Object, or a string, depending on the value of the request's responseType property.

js:XMLHttpRequest:responseText.description: The read-only XMLHttpRequest property responseText returns the text received from a server following a request being sent.

js:XMLHttpRequest:responseType.description: The XMLHttpRequest property responseType is an enumerated string value specifying the type of data contained in the response.

js:XMLHttpRequest:responseURL.description: The read-only XMLHttpRequest.responseURL property returns the serialized URL of the response or the empty string if the URL is null. If the URL is returned, any URL fragment present in the URL will be stripped away. The value of responseURL will be the final URL obtained after any redirects.

js:XMLHttpRequest:responseXML.description: The XMLHttpRequest.responseXML read-only property returns a Document containing the HTML or XML retrieved by the request; or null if the request was unsuccessful, has not yet been sent, or if the data can't be parsed as XML or HTML.

js:XMLHttpRequest:status.description: The read-only XMLHttpRequest.status property returns the numerical HTTP status code of the XMLHttpRequest's response.

js:XMLHttpRequest:statusText.description: The read-only XMLHttpRequest.statusText property returns a string containing the response's status message as returned by the HTTP server. Unlike XMLHttpRequest.status which indicates a numerical status code, this property contains the text of the response status, such as "OK" or "Not Found". If the request's readyState is in UNSENT or OPENED state, the value of statusText will be an empty string.

js:XMLHttpRequest:timeout.description: The XMLHttpRequest.timeout property is an unsigned long representing the number of milliseconds a request can take before automatically being terminated. The default value is 0, which means there is no timeout. Timeout shouldn't be used for synchronous XMLHttpRequests requests used in a document environment or it will throw an InvalidAccessError exception. When a timeout happens, a timeout event is fired.

js:XMLHttpRequest:upload.description: The XMLHttpRequest upload property returns an XMLHttpRequestUpload object that can be observed to monitor an upload's progress.

js:XMLHttpRequest:withCredentials.description: The XMLHttpRequest.withCredentials property is a boolean value that indicates whether or not cross-site Access-Control requests should be made using credentials such as cookies, authentication headers or TLS client certificates. Setting withCredentials has no effect on same-origin requests.

js:XMLHttpRequest:abort.description: The XMLHttpRequest.abort() method aborts the request if it has already been sent. When a request is aborted, its readyState is changed to XMLHttpRequest.UNSENT (0) and the request's status code is set to 0.

js:XMLHttpRequest:getAllResponseHeaders.description: The XMLHttpRequest method getAllResponseHeaders() returns all the response headers, separated by CRLF, as a string, or returns null if no response has been received.

js:XMLHttpRequest:getResponseHeader.description: The XMLHttpRequest method getResponseHeader() returns the string containing the text of a particular header's value.

js:XMLHttpRequest:open.description: The XMLHttpRequest method open() initializes a newly-created request, or re-initializes an existing one.
js:XMLHttpRequest:open.syntax: open(method: string, url: string | URL): void

js:XMLHttpRequest:overrideMimeType.description: The XMLHttpRequest method overrideMimeType() specifies a MIME type other than the one provided by the server to be used instead when interpreting the data being transferred in a request.

js:XMLHttpRequest:send.description: The XMLHttpRequest method send() sends the request to the server.

js:XMLHttpRequest:setRequestHeader.description: The XMLHttpRequest method setRequestHeader() sets the value of an HTTP request header. When using setRequestHeader(), you must call it after calling open(), but before calling send(). If this method is called several times with the same header, the values are merged into one single request header.

js:XMLSerializer:serializeToString.description: The XMLSerializer method serializeToString() constructs a string representing the specified DOM tree in XML form.

js:XPathExpression:evaluate.description: The evaluate() method of the XPathExpression interface executes an XPath expression on the given node or document and returns an XPathResult.
js:XPathExpression:evaluate.syntax: evaluate(contextNode: Node, type?: number, result?: XPathResult | null): XPathResult

js:XPathResult:booleanValue.description: The read-only booleanValue property of the XPathResult interface returns the boolean value of a result with XPathResult.resultType being BOOLEAN_TYPE.

js:XPathResult:invalidIteratorState.description: The read-only invalidIteratorState property of the XPathResult interface signifies that the iterator has become invalid. It is true if XPathResult.resultType is UNORDERED_NODE_ITERATOR_TYPE or ORDERED_NODE_ITERATOR_TYPE and the document has been modified since this result was returned.

js:XPathResult:numberValue.description: The read-only numberValue property of the XPathResult interface returns the numeric value of a result with XPathResult.resultType being NUMBER_TYPE.

js:XPathResult:resultType.description: The read-only resultType property of the XPathResult interface represents the type of the result, as defined by the type constants.

js:XPathResult:singleNodeValue.description: The read-only singleNodeValue property of the XPathResult interface returns a Node value or null in case no node was matched of a result with XPathResult.resultType being ANY_UNORDERED_NODE_TYPE or FIRST_ORDERED_NODE_TYPE.

js:XPathResult:snapshotLength.description: The read-only snapshotLength property of the XPathResult interface represents the number of nodes in the result snapshot.

js:XPathResult:stringValue.description: The read-only stringValue property of the XPathResult interface returns the string value of a result with XPathResult.resultType being STRING_TYPE.

js:XPathResult:iterateNext.description: The iterateNext() method of the XPathResult interface iterates over a node set result and returns the next node from it or null if there are no more nodes.

js:XPathResult:snapshotItem.description: The snapshotItem() method of the XPathResult interface returns an item of the snapshot collection or null in case the index is not within the range of nodes. Unlike the iterator result, the snapshot does not become invalid, but may not correspond to the current document if it is mutated.

js:XSLTProcessor:clearParameters.description: The clearParameters() method of the XSLTProcessor interface removes all parameters (<xsl:param>) and their values from the stylesheet imported in the processor. The XSLTProcessor will then use the default values specified in the XSLT stylesheet.

js:XSLTProcessor:getParameter.description: The getParameter() method of the XSLTProcessor interface returns the value of a parameter (<xsl:param>) from the stylesheet imported in the processor.
js:XSLTProcessor:getParameter.syntax: getParameter(namespaceURI: string | null, localName: string): any

js:XSLTProcessor:importStylesheet.description: The importStylesheet() method of the XSLTProcessor interface imports an XSLT stylesheet for the processor.

js:XSLTProcessor:removeParameter.description: The removeParameter() method of the XSLTProcessor interface removes the parameter (<xsl:param>) and its value from the stylesheet imported in the processor.
js:XSLTProcessor:removeParameter.syntax: removeParameter(namespaceURI: string | null, localName: string): void

js:XSLTProcessor:reset.description: The reset() method of the XSLTProcessor interface removes all parameters (<xsl:param>) and the XSLT stylesheet from the processor. The XSLTProcessor will then be in its original state when it was created.

js:XSLTProcessor:setParameter.description: The setParameter() method of the XSLTProcessor interface sets the value of a parameter (<xsl:param>) in the stylesheet imported in the processor.
js:XSLTProcessor:setParameter.syntax: setParameter(namespaceURI: string | null, localName: string, value: any): void

js:XSLTProcessor:transformToDocument.description: The transformToDocument() method of the XSLTProcessor interface transforms the provided Node source to a Document using the XSLT stylesheet associated with XSLTProcessor.

js:XSLTProcessor:transformToFragment.description: The transformToFragment() method of the XSLTProcessor interface transforms a provided Node source to a DocumentFragment using the XSLT stylesheet associated with the XSLTProcessor.

js:Console:assert.description: The console.assert() static method writes an error message to the console if the assertion is false. If the assertion is true, nothing happens.

js:Console:clear.description: The console.clear() static method clears the console if possible.

js:Console:count.description: The console.count() static method logs the number of times that this particular call to count() has been called.

js:Console:countReset.description: The console.countReset() static method resets counter used with console.count().

js:Console:debug.description: The console.debug() static method outputs a message to the console at the "debug" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display debug output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. This log level might correspond to the Debug or Verbose log level.

js:Console:dir.description: The console.dir() static method displays a list of the properties of the specified JavaScript object. In browser consoles, the output is presented as a hierarchical listing with disclosure triangles that let you see the contents of child objects.

js:Console:dirxml.description: The console.dirxml() static method displays an interactive tree of the descendant elements of the specified XML/HTML element. If it is not possible to display as an element the JavaScript Object view is shown instead. The output is presented as a hierarchical listing of expandable nodes that let you see the contents of child nodes.

js:Console:error.description: The console.error() static method outputs a message to the console at the "error" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display error output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. The message may be formatted as an error, with red colors and call stack information.

js:Console:group.description: The console.group() static method creates a new inline group in the Web console log, causing any subsequent console messages to be indented by an additional level, until console.groupEnd() is called.

js:Console:groupCollapsed.description: The console.groupCollapsed() static method creates a new inline group in the console. Unlike console.group(), however, the new group is created collapsed. The user will need to use the disclosure button next to it to expand it, revealing the entries created in the group.

js:Console:groupEnd.description: The console.groupEnd() static method exits the current inline group in the console. See Using groups in the console in the console documentation for details and examples.

js:Console:info.description: The console.info() static method outputs a message to the console at the "info" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display info output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. The message may receive special formatting, such as a small "i" icon next to it.

js:Console:log.description: The console.log() static method outputs a message to the console.

js:Console:table.description: The console.table() static method displays tabular data as a table.

js:Console:time.description: The console.time() static method starts a timer you can use to track how long an operation takes. You give each timer a unique name, and may have up to 10,000 timers running on a given page. When you call console.timeEnd() with the same name, the browser will output the time, in milliseconds, that elapsed since the timer was started.

js:Console:timeEnd.description: The console.timeEnd() static method stops a timer that was previously started by calling console.time().

js:Console:timeLog.description: The console.timeLog() static method logs the current value of a timer that was previously started by calling console.time().

js:Console:timeStamp.description: The console.timeStamp() static method adds a single marker to the browser's Performance tool (Firefox bug 1387528, Chrome). This lets you correlate a point in your code with the other events recorded in the timeline, such as layout and paint events.

js:Console:trace.description: The console.trace() static method outputs a stack trace to the console.

js:Console:warn.description: The console.warn() static method outputs a warning message to the console at the "warning" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display warning output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. The message may receive special formatting, such as yellow colors and a warning icon.

js:FormData:entries.description: Returns an array of key, value pairs for every entry in the list.

js:FormData:keys.description: Returns a list of keys in the list.

js:FormData:values.description: Returns a list of values in the list.

js:Headers:entries.description: Returns an iterator allowing to go through all key/value pairs contained in this object.

js:Headers:keys.description: Returns an iterator allowing to go through all keys of the key/value pairs contained in this object.

js:Headers:values.description: Returns an iterator allowing to go through all values of the key/value pairs contained in this object.

js:NodeList:entries.description: Returns an array of key, value pairs for every entry in the list.

js:NodeList:keys.description: Returns an list of keys in the list.

js:NodeList:values.description: Returns an list of values in the list.

js:NodeListOf:entries.description: Returns an array of key, value pairs for every entry in the list.

js:NodeListOf:keys.description: Returns an list of keys in the list.

js:NodeListOf:values.description: Returns an list of values in the list.

js:URLSearchParams:entries.description: Returns an array of key, value pairs for every entry in the search params.

js:URLSearchParams:keys.description: Returns a list of keys in the search params.

js:URLSearchParams:values.description: Returns a list of values in the search params.
